notice: The five ice-age maps of Grind Strat (about 10,000, 9,500, 8,500, 7,500 and 5,000 BC): water and ice on a 1 km grid, land cover on a 2 km grid, with the east hatched "no model yet" for the four oldest. Rough previews made by rules from the open data below, not measurements. Shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Sources: Ice-age water and ice: shore-displacement model © SGU (Geological Survey of Sweden), released as open data (CC0) (CC0 1.0, creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/); Ice sheet at about 10,000 BC: the DATED-1 reconstruction by Hughes and others (2016) (CC BY 3.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/); Forest around 9,750 to 9,250 BC: a pollen-based land-cover map by Behnaz Pirzamanbein, from Githumbi, Pirzamanbein et al. (2022) (CC BY-SA 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); Forest around 8,750 to 8,250 BC: a pollen-based land-cover map by Behnaz Pirzamanbein, from Githumbi, Pirzamanbein et al. (2022) (CC BY-SA 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); Forest around 7,750 to 7,250 BC: a pollen-based land-cover map by Behnaz Pirzamanbein, from Githumbi, Pirzamanbein et al. (2022) (CC BY-SA 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); Forest around 5,250 to 4,750 BC: a pollen-based land-cover map by Behnaz Pirzamanbein, from Githumbi, Pirzamanbein et al. (2022) (CC BY-SA 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).

labels.water: Water: SGU's shore-displacement model (Påsse and Daniels 2015), the table nearest each age, moved onto 1 km cells. Its small modelled lakes are left out. The 100-year tables can be off by up to about 500 years.
labels.ice10000: Ice at about 10,000 BC: DATED-1's most-credible ice margin at 12 thousand years ago (Hughes and others 2016), a reconstruction, not a measurement.
labels.iceSgu: Ice at the later ages: the ice sheet of SGU's model, a simplified model of the melting.
labels.cover10000: Painted by a rule, not from a pollen map: open herb and grass land with birch, juniper and willow (Stančikaitė 2006), shown as tundra.
labels.cover: Land cover from the pollen map (SpatioCompo: REVEALS cover of conifer forest, broadleaved forest and open land, in which birch counts as broadleaved and pine's plentiful pollen is corrected for; 1 degree cells blended smoothly) turned into four classes by a rule of ours: in the three cold ages, open land that is half the land or more is tundra; otherwise forest, where conifers that are half the forest or more are pine; below that, where the broadleaved trees are birch (9,500 and 8,500 BC), a conifer share of 40% or less is birch woodland and the rest is mixed (birch and pine); later (7,500 and 5,000 BC) the broadleaved trees are birch with hazel and elm, then lime and oak, and the rest is mixed forest.
labels.hatch: Hatched "no model yet": land east of SGU's model for the four oldest ages (the model's east edge runs from about 26.2E at 55N to about 27.5E at 59N).
labels.east5000: East of the model at about 5,000 BC the sea is a rough estimate: the Gulf of Finland carried on east, up to 150 km, over land now 10 m or less above the sea, the middle of the Litorina Sea's highest shore in the Narva-Luga area (6 to 14 m, Rosentau and others 2013), so about 4 m either way (TO CHECK). Lakes there are not drawn.
